note: Experiment output. Not published; not a release for the repeat rule.

classificationRules.Trending: sound check: >=5 distinct creators posted with the sound in the last 14 days AND >=5 sampled videos have >=100K plays
classificationRules.Rising: sound check: 3-4 distinct creators in the last 14 days, sound first sampled use within the last 120 days
classificationRules.Breakout: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading
classificationRules.Sustained: UNAVAILABLE until 5 consecutive weekly snapshots exist

rejectedAfterReview.classificationByRules: Trending (9 creators in 7 days, 9 of 10 samples at 100K+)
rejectedAfterReview.reason: content rule: the joke is sexual innuendo ("Send?" / "A picture of your hair?"). Watched via embed.
cover shows a two-person rap lip-sync performance; commercial track (audioRisk HIGH); trend dates to 2022. CORRECTS Test #1, which included it.
fails the new breakout rule (plays are 3.7x followers, under 5x) and the sound is not spreading. Removed from Test #1's list.

rejectedAfterReview.item: Thank-you-dad B&W photo trend (2 creators, 2 different sounds)
rejectedAfterReview.reason: personal tribute storytelling, not adaptable for businesses; sources are 22-23s tutorials

records.name: Couple glow-up transition
records.classificationRule: sound check: >=5 distinct creators posted with the sound in the last 14 days AND >=5 sampled videos have >=100K plays

ourAssessment.whySelected: Verified multi-creator trend, and the mechanic (plain → dressed up on a hand clasp) works for anyone selling a transformation.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-5s: you (and a partner or teammate) in plain clothes, facing camera. 5-6s: clasp hands and spin on the beat. 6-12s: same spot, fully styled.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Apparel, jewellery, beauty: the "after" is wearing your product.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Stylists and MUAs: client + stylist, messy → finished. Two-person teams: work clothes → event-ready.

visualCheck.saw: two people in casual clothes, hands clasp and spin, both reappear in formal wear

records.name: Makeup glow-up transition
records.classificationRule: sound check: >=5 distinct creators posted with the sound in the last 14 days AND >=5 sampled videos have >=100K plays

ourAssessment.whySelected: Verified trend: 7 creators used this sound in the last 14 days and all 10 sampled uses have 100K+ plays. The before → after is the whole format.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-4s: bare face (or plain product), looking at camera. 4-5s: sweep your hand across the lens. 5-9s: finished look, same framing.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Beauty and skincare: bare → wearing your product. Any product: plain → styled, using the hand sweep.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: MUAs, estheticians, lash and brow artists: client before → after (with permission).
cautions: Same format family as the couple glow-up and upside-down flip: do not publish all three in one week (soft duplicate by formatTag).

visualCheck.saw: bare face with glasses, a hand passes in front of the lens, full glam with hair down

records.name: Two-person outfit transition
records.classificationRule: sound check: >=5 distinct creators posted with the sound in the last 14 days AND >=5 sampled videos have >=100K plays

ourAssessment.whySelected: Verified trend on a new sound (first sampled use mid-August, 5 creators in the last 14 days). Two people plus two outfits, nothing else.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-4s: two people side by side in loungewear. 4-5s: kick or jump on the beat. 5-9s: both in the "after" looks. Camera locked off.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Boutiques and apparel: before → your pieces.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Local teams: street clothes → uniform ("clocking in"). Salons: before → after appointment.
ourAssessment.onScreenText: "Us before vs after opening the shop"
cautions: Needs a second person and a quick outfit change.
The example creator has 6.9M followers, so this video is not a breakout. The trend evidence is the sound spread.

visualCheck.saw: two people in loungewear in a kitchen, a kick on the beat, both reappear styled (red gown, sharp outfit)

records.name: Upside-down makeup flip
records.classificationRule: sound check: 3-4 distinct creators in the last 14 days, sound first sampled use within the last 120 days

ourAssessment.whySelected: Rising sound (3 creators in the last 14 days, first sampled use late August). A simple before → after with one camera move.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-5s: the "before". 5-6s: turn the phone upside down (or cover the lens) on the beat. 6-11s: the finished look.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Beauty: bare → wearing it. Food: raw → plated.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: MUAs, nail techs, barbers: bare → finished.
cautions: Same format family as the makeup glow-up. The exact camera move needs a human look.

visualCheck.saw: bare face with hair tied up, a black transition frame, full glam with curly hair down. The flip mechanic itself is inferred from #upsidedown.

records.name: Satisfying process close-up
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 2.3M plays from about 1K followers. A tight close-up of one satisfying step of making something.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-10s: extreme close-up of the most satisfying step (icing, peeling film, erasing, polishing, pouring). No talking.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Makers, bakers, candle and soap makers, artists.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Cleaners (the wipe), detailers (the foam), landscapers (the edge).
cautions: "b2b" is an older, widely used sound; any calm track works.

visualCheck.saw: cover: a pencil portrait; caption says erasing is the satisfying part

records.name: 5-second transformation
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 1.1M plays from a 279-follower account, with 26,129 shares. Five seconds, no talking.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-2s: before, quick and unposed. 2-5s: the result, one clean shot.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Skincare, cleaning products, tools: the result in 5 seconds.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Hair stylists first; also groomers, detailers, cleaners.
ourAssessment.onScreenText: "New [hair / car / kitchen] for a new season"
cautions: Client permission before posting their face.

visualCheck.saw: cover shows the finished result (long wavy hair). The before half was not seen.

records.name: "Drops [date]" outfit tease
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 841K plays at 24x the brand's followers. A person simply wearing the new piece plus a date overlay.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-10s: someone wearing or holding the new product, glancing around casually. Overlay: "Drops [date] 👀".
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Apparel, accessories, any launch with a date.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: New service or menu with a start date.
cautions: Established sound; the evidence is this one video.

visualCheck.saw: cover: a model in the new black tank and jeans with overlay "Drops 9/24 ♥️👀". CORRECTS Test #1 (no finger-to-lips, no covered product).

records.name: Short clip + "why I started" text story
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 599K plays from 578 followers and 8,346 saves. Found again by the "digital product launch" search.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-6s: one calm shot of you. The story goes in on-screen text and the caption.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: Digital products: "a few years ago I was [problem], so I started [product]".
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Coaches and consultants: the same, about the outcome you help with.
ourAssessment.onScreenText: "A few years ago, I was [relatable struggle]…"

records.name: "Tomorrow." playful drop teaser
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 495K plays from 1,938 followers and 16,308 shares. It shows the product in a fun, casual shoot plus "Tomorrow." Easy for any launch.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-7s: a fun, unpolished clip of your new product in use (behind the scenes of your shoot is perfect). 7-10s: text "Tomorrow." plus the time.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Opening a limited number of booking slots; show yourself setting up.
ourAssessment.onScreenText: "Tomorrow. Limited. Once it's gone, it's gone."

visualCheck.saw: cover: a model in the new pink activewear, playful, in a white studio holding a ball. CORRECTS Test #1, which assumed a dark teaser that hid the product.

records.name: Nail set transition
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 476K plays at 173x followers. The creator jokes the transition beat the nails, so the transition is the hook.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-5s: bare nails close to the lens. 5-6s: hand sweep or snap on the beat. 6-13s: finished set, same angle.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Nail techs; the same mechanic for lashes and brows.
cautions: The sound (nailz_forever64) is widely used but not currently spreading (2 creators in 14 days).

visualCheck.saw: cover: close-up of the finished long nails. The transition itself was not seen.

records.name: "Nothing against influencers, but…" owner POV
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 443K plays at 217x followers. An honest owner POV works for any small business.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-9s: you doing an everyday task with the POV text on screen. No talking.
ourAssessment.productAdaptation: "…I'd have to sell [X] just to pay them."
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: "…that's [X] clients just to pay an agency."
ourAssessment.onScreenText: "Guess I'm the face of my brand now 😂"
cautions: Track "What's This? What's That?": check availability on business accounts, or substitute a playful sound.

visualCheck.saw: cover: the owner with text overlay and a tray of cookies

records.name: "I hate packaging [product]" honest packing clip
records.classificationRule: the example video passes the breakout rule (>=100K plays and >=5x followers, floor 1,000; or >=1M plays and >=1x followers). Sound not shown to be spreading

ourAssessment.whySelected: Breakout: 396K plays at 396x followers (floored). An honest, unglamorous behind-the-scenes shot of packing orders.
ourAssessment.filmThis: 0-7s: you packing orders, slightly fed up, with text "I hate packaging [product]". Use a comedic sound.
ourAssessment.serviceAdaptation: Swap for the task you dread: "I hate invoicing".
cautions: The sound's content was not heard; pick your own comedic sound.
